title: Control: standard education with leaflet: Comparative Evaluation of Immersive Virtual Reality and Mobile Patient Education in the Context of CAR-T Cell Therapy for Autoimmune Diseases Prior to the Initiation of Chimeric Antibody Receptor Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Polymyositis, and Systemic Sclerosis; Version: Chimeric Antibody Receptor Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Polymyositis, and Systemic Sclerosis Virtual Reality (CARSLE VR) App – Fighting Lupus 1.0 and CARSLE Mobile App 1.0
summary: In some serious diseases, the body's own immune system attacks healthy tissue such as the skin, muscles, joints or internal organs. When standard medications are not effective enough, a new treatment has been available since 2021: The patient's own immune cells are extracted from their blood and modified in the laboratory so that they can specifically target and neutralize the misdirected immune cells. Afterward, the person receives the modified cells back via a single infusion. This treatment is new, innovative and complex. Patients often find it hard to understand all the information and to make a well-considered decision for or against it. The study examines whether digital information formats, in addition to a patient education with a physician, help patients feel well-informed and more confident in their decisions. It also investigates whether virtual reality glasses that display a three-dimensional virtual world are more helpful in this regard than the same content on a tablet. About 60 patients at the Department of Medicine 3 of Universitätsklinikum Erlangen will take part at the study. They are divided into three groups. Everyone receives the classical patient education with a physician and an information leaflet. The first group is given the information flyer again later to read. The second group also uses the virtual reality glasses to explore a virtual world. It explains step by step how the disease develops and how the treatment works. The physician is present in the virtual world as a virtual figure. The third group goes through the same content on a tablet together with a physician. After treatment, the second and third groups may choose to use the application again on their own. Short questionnaires at several points in time measure how confident participants feel about their decision, how well informed they feel and how well they understood the content. Whether a participant decides for or against treatment is not studied.
conditions: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Polymyositis, Systemic Sclerosis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Patients who are to be treated with CAR-T cell therapy
•    Patients diagnosed with SLE, IIM, or SSc for whom, based on a physician’s assessment, CAR-T cell therapy is being considered as part of the underlying clinical trial due to an inadequate response to established treatment options.
Exclusion criteria:
•    Inability to give informed consent
•    Epilepsy
•    Acute neurological disorders
•    Severe visual impairments
•    Minors
•    Pregnant women
•    Individuals with binocular vision disorders
•    Previous participation in a study that involved the use of the CARSLE VR application
